name: SikaBond-115 Max Tack
paste:
SIKABOND®-115 MAX TACK: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaBond®-115 Max Tack, April 2023, Version 01.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/s/sikabond-115-maxtack.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaBond®-115 Max Tack where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02).
1.2 Product description. SikaBond®-115 Max Tack is a 1-part construction adhesive with high final strength which bonds most construction material substrates. Internal and sheltered outdoor use.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. An adhesive to bond most construction components such as:
    - Skirting boards
    - Wooden frames
    - Battens
    - Mouldings
    - Panels,
    - Terracotta tiles
    - Anodised aluminium
    - Polystyrene mouldings and ceiling tiles
    - Concrete, mortar, fibre cement, wood and paint
    An adhesive to bond most construction materials such as:
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.8.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaBond®-115 Max Tack
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: INTERIOR GRAB ADHESIVE
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Sustainability.
    - Conformity with LEED v4 EQc 2: Low-Emitting Materials
    - VOC emission classification GEV-EMICODE EC 1PLUS
    - VOC emission classification of building materials RTS M1
    - Class A+ according to French Regulation on VOC emissions
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - ISO 1183-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Density (p.2).
    - ISO 868: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shore A hardness (p.2).
    - EN 1465: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shear strength (p.2).
    - ISO 7390: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Sag flow (p.2).
    - CQP 049-2: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where: Application Information > Curing rate (p.2).
    - CQP 019-1: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where: Application Information > Skinning time (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Easy to apply
    - Easy to clean
    - Rapid build-up of strength
    - High final strength
    - Very low emissions
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Acrylic dispersion
    - Colour: White
    - Density: ~1.40 kg/l (ISO 1183-1)
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Shore A hardness: ~94 (after 28 days) (ISO 868)
    - Tensile strength: ~6.0 N/mm² (ISO 37)
    - Tensile strain at break: ~35 % (ISO 37)
    - Shear strength: ~4.4 N/mm², 0.1 mm adhesive thickness (EN 1465)
    - Service temperature: −15 °C min. / +60 °C max.
2.7 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 290ml Cartridge; 100g Mini Ssg
    - Shelf life: 18 months from the date of production.
    - Storage conditions: The product must be stored in original, unopened and undamaged packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +25 °C. Always refer to packaging.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate preparation.
    - The substrate must be sound, clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, cement laitance, old sealants and poorly bonded paint coatings which could affect adhesion of the adhesive.
    - Removal techniques such as wire brushing, grinding, sanding or other suitable mechanical tools can be used.
    - All dust, loose and friable material must be completely removed from all surfaces before application of primers or adhesive.
    - For optimum adhesion and critical, high performance applications the following priming and/or pre-treatment procedures shall be followed:
    - Non-porous substrates
    - Aluminium, anodised aluminium, stainless steel, PVC, galvanised steel, powder coated metals or glazed tiles. Slightly roughen surface with a fine abrasive pad. Clean and pre-treat using Sika® Aktivator-205 applied with a clean cloth.
    - Before application of adhesive, allow a waiting time of > 15 minutes (< 6 hours).
    - Other metals, such as copper, brass and titanium-zinc, cleaned and pre-treat using Sika® Aktivator-205 applied with a clean cloth. After a waiting time of > 15 minutes (< 6 hours). Apply Sika® Primer-3 N applied by brush. Allow a further waiting time of > 30 minutes (< 8 hours) before application of adhesive.
    - Porous substrates
    - Concrete, aerated concrete and cement-based renders, mortars and bricks. Prime surface using Sika® Primer-3 N applied by brush.
    - Before application of adhesive, allow a waiting time of > 30 minutes (< 8 hours).
    - For more detailed advice and instructions contact Sika Technical Services.
    - Note: Primers are adhesion promoters and not an alternative to improve poor preparation / cleaning of the bonded surface. Primers also improve the long-term adhesion performance of the bonded surfaces.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Sag flow: 0 mm (20 mm profile,+23 °C) (ISO 7390)
    - Skinning time: ~30 minutes (+23 °C / 50 % r.h.) (CQP 019-1)
4.3 Yield.
    | Yield | Dimension |
    | 1 Cartridge (290 ml) |
    | ~100 spots | Diameter = 30 mm |
    | Thickness = 4 mm |
    | ~15 m bead | Nozzle diameter = 5 mm |
    | (~20 ml per linear metre) |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
4.4 Curing rate.
    | ~6 mm / 24 hours | Sika Corporate Quality Procedure |
    | (+23 °C / 50 % r.h.) |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (CQP 049-2)
4.5 Instructions. For the application of SikaBond®-115 Max Tack all generally accepted rules of building and construction apply.
4.6 Mixing.
    - Ready to use product APPLICATION METHOD / TOOLS
    - After the necessary substrate preparation, prepare the end of the SikaBond®-115 Max Tack cartridge, insert into the sealant gun and fit the nozzle.
    - Apply in beads, strips or spots at intervals of a few centimetres each. If necessary, use a notched trowel to distribute SikaBond®-115 Max Tack evenly.
    - Use hand pressure only to fix the components to be bonded into position before skinning of the adhesive occurs. Incorrectly positioned components can easily be unbonded and repositioned during the first few minutes after application. If necessary, use temporary adhesive tapes, wedges, or supports to hold the assembled components together during the initial curing time. The recommended adhesive layer thickness (depending on surface evenness) is < 3 mm. For immediate grab fixing, the thickness of the adhesive layer must be ≤ 1 mm.
    - Fresh, uncured adhesive remaining on the surface must be removed immediately. Final strength will be reached after complete curing, i.e. 24 to 48 hours at +23 °C, depending on the environmental conditions and adhesive layer thickness.
4.7 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment immediately after use with Sika® Remover-208. Once cured, hardened material can only be removed mechanically. For cleaning skin use Sika® Cleaning Wipes-100.
4.8 Limitations and important considerations.
    - For good workability, the adhesive temperature should be +20 °C.
    - Application during high temperature changes is not recommended (movement during curing).
    - Before bonding, check adhesion and resistance of paints and coatings by carrying out a trial.
    - SikaBond®-115 Max Tack can be overpainted with most conventional water-based coating and paint systems. However, paints must first be tested to ensure compatibility by carrying out preliminary trials. The best over-painting results are obtained when the adhesive is allowed to fully cure first. Note: non-flexible paint systems may impair the elasticity of the adhesive and lead to cracking of the paint film.
    - Colour variations may occur due to exposure to chemicals, high temperatures and/or UV-radiation (especially with the colour shade white). However, a change in colour is purely of aesthetic nature and does not adversely influence the technical performance or durability of the product.
    - Always use SikaBond®-115 Max Tack in conjunction with mechanical fixings for overhead applications of heavy components.
    - For very heavy components provide temporary support until SikaBond®-115 Max Tack has fully cured.
    - For optimum bonding, at least one of the two substrates must be porous.
    - Before using on natural stone, contact Sika Technical Services.
    - Do not use on bituminous substrates, natural rubber, EPDM rubber or on any building materials which might leech oils, plasticisers or solvents that could degrade the adhesive.
    - Do not use on polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE / Teflon), and certain plasticised synthetic materials (pre-trials shall be carried out or contact Sika Technical Services).
    - Do not use for bonding glass if the bond line is exposed to sunlight.
    - Do not use for structural bonding.
4.9 Further information.
    - Pre-treatment Sealing and Bonding Chart

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +5 °C min. / +35 °C max.
5.3 Substrate temperature. +5 °C min. / +35 °C max., ≥ +3 °C above dew point temperature
5.4 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.8):
    - For good workability, the adhesive temperature should be +20 °C.
    - Application during high temperature changes is not recommended (movement during curing).
    - Colour variations may occur due to exposure to chemicals, high temperatures and/or UV-radiation (especially with the colour shade white). However, a change in colour is purely of aesthetic nature and does not adversely influence the technical performance or durability of the product.
5.5 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - Before bonding, check adhesion and resistance of paints and coatings by carrying out a trial.
5.6 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Density: ~1.40 kg/l (ISO 1183-1)
    - Shore A hardness: ~94 (after 28 days) (ISO 868)
    - Tensile strength: ~6.0 N/mm² (ISO 37)
    - Tensile strain at break: ~35 % (ISO 37)
    - Shear strength: ~4.4 N/mm², 0.1 mm adhesive thickness (EN 1465)
    - Sag flow: 0 mm (20 mm profile,+23 °C) (ISO 7390)
    - Curing rate: ~6 mm / 24 hours | Sika Corporate Quality Procedure; (+23 °C / 50 % r.h.) (CQP 049-2)
    - Skinning time: ~30 minutes (+23 °C / 50 % r.h.) (CQP 019-1)
5.7 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.8 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaBond®-115 Max Tack, April 2023, Version 01.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/s/sikabond-115-maxtack.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS SikaBond®-115 Max Tack, version 17/06/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/2/sds-sikabond-115maxtack.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
